QF.id: AIFM Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_6

question.text: Narmada Growth AIF holds four portfolio companies with the following weights and expected returns: Co. A (weight 25%, E(r) 10%), Co. B (weight 15%, E(r) 14%), Co. C (weight 35%, E(r) 18%), Co. D (weight 25%, E(r) 22%). What is the expected return of the portfolio?

explanation.text: The Logic: Expected portfolio return is the weighted average of the expected returns of the constituent assets: E(Rp) = ΣWi·E(Ri). Plugging in: 0.25×10% + 0.15×14% + 0.35×18% + 0.25×22% = 2.50% + 2.10% + 6.30% + 5.50% = 16.40%. The Trap: 16.00% is the simple arithmetic average of the four returns and ignores the weights. 14.50% drops the contribution of one of the assets. 15.30% transposes two weights, giving a similar-looking but incorrect answer. Note: The portfolio expected return is simply the weight-by-return sum across all assets; check that weights sum to 1 and that each weight is multiplied by its own asset's expected return before adding.
